brief.offer: Onboarding email sequences for startup founders

facts.claim: Mercury launched Mercury Books, AI-powered accounting software that categorizes and reconciles transactions as they happen.
facts.excerpt: Today, we're launching @Mercury Books. AI-powered accounting software, for your bookkeeper or you, that categorizes and reconciles your transactions the moment they happen.

facts.claim: Mercury is a fintech company offering banking services through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., rather than being an FDIC-insured bank itself.
facts.excerpt: Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.
facts.source_title: Online Business Banking For Startups, Small Businesses & Scaling Companies

facts.excerpt: Today, more than 300,000 customers use Mercury.

facts.claim: By the end of 2025, 73% of Mercury's new customers came from outside the AI or tech startup category.
facts.excerpt: By the end of 2025, 73% of new customers came from outside the AI or tech startup category,

facts.claim: One in three U.S. startups uses Mercury, and Mercury onboarded 2.4 times more AI companies in 2025 than in the previous year.
facts.excerpt: Today, 1 in 3 U.S. startups use Mercury, including a rapidly growing share of AI companies — in 2025, we onboarded 2.4x more AI companies than the year before.

facts.claim: Mercury Insights offers business accounts AI-powered cashflow alerts and a chatbot for questions about their financial data.
facts.excerpt: filter and compare by time periods, get AI-powered cashflow alerts and ask a chatbot questions like “Why did expenses increase this month?”

facts.claim: Mercury Bill Pay automates accounts payable, organizing bills by approval status and due date and supporting scheduled ACH, check, or wire payments.
facts.excerpt: Bills sent to your dedicated inbox are automatically organized by approval status and due date, and can be scheduled for payment via ACH, check, or wire.

facts.claim: Mercury offers unlimited invoicing in its free version, while recurring invoices and ACH debit invoicing are available in paid plans.
facts.excerpt: Customers can create, send, track, and receive payment on as many invoices as they’d like in the free version of Mercury. Advanced invoicing capabilities, such as sending recurring invoices, and invoicing with ACH debit, are available as part of our paid plans.

research.website_note: The mercury.com homepage identifies Mercury and its services, and company profiles link to mercury.com as Mercury’s website.

strategy.observation: Mercury launched Mercury Books, adding AI-powered accounting software that categorizes and reconciles transactions as they happen.
strategy.offer_link: Founder-focused onboarding emails could introduce Mercury Books to startup customers, explain its categorization and reconciliation capabilities, and guide interested founders toward first use. This gives the Lifecycle Marketing Lead a product-launch-specific application for the sender’s offer.
hypotheses: Startup founders may be an intended audience for Mercury Books.
The Lifecycle Marketing Lead may own or influence email onboarding for the new product.
Some founders may need guidance to move from awareness of Mercury Books to using it.
strategy.angle: With Mercury Books launched, are you building a dedicated onboarding email sequence to help startup founders move from hearing about it to using it?
strategy.fit_reason: The launch creates a plausible need for product-specific onboarding, and email sequences are directly relevant to a lifecycle marketing role; the founder audience and recipient’s ownership still need confirmation.

draft.subject: Founder onboarding for Mercury Books
draft.body:
Hi,

With Mercury Books launched, my guess is some startup founders will need a little guidance between hearing about it and trying it.

I write onboarding email sequences for startup founders, with each message guiding them toward a clear first step. If founders are an audience you’re targeting for Books, a dedicated sequence could help interested customers get started without packing all the guidance into the launch email.

Are you planning a separate onboarding sequence for founders interested in Books?
